terms.meaning: a rule that the corrected value never falls as the predicted value rises
a band of predicted chances, here 10 percentage points wide

the typical size of random noise in a measured rate

sections.name: File setup, Sample, IsotonicMap
sections.title: Sample and map shapes
sections.what: Describes one sample: predicted chance, what happened (0 or 1), and an optional weight. Also describes the saved map of points.
sections.why: Likely reason: a shared format for the training data and the saved correction.
sections.watch_out: The weight is optional and counts as 1 when missing, so a sample with no weight counts fully.

sections.name: fitIsotonic
sections.title: Fitting the correction map
sections.what: Sorts samples by predicted chance, groups them, and merges neighbours whenever the earlier group has a higher observed rate than the later one, so the result never falls. Returns the points.
sections.why: Likely reason: the standard way to correct probabilities without assuming a fixed shape.
sections.watch_out: Empty input throws, and very few samples give a jagged map that may not generalise.

sections.name: applyIsotonic, Bucket
sections.title: Applying the correction and band type
sections.what: Turns a predicted chance into a corrected one by straight-line steps between points, and holds the first and last values flat beyond the ends. Defines the shape of one band's results.
sections.why: Likely reason: smooth between points, flat at the ends, so nothing is extrapolated.
sections.watch_out: Values beyond the fitted range are held at the nearest end, so the correction cannot predict past the data.

sections.name: buckets
sections.title: Grouping results into 10-point bands
sections.what: Splits samples into ten bands from 0 to 100 percent. For each band reports the count, average predicted chance, observed rate and the gap in points.
sections.why: Likely reason: both the reliability chart and the gate need these bands.
sections.watch_out: The top band includes exactly 100 percent, while the others exclude their upper edge.

sections.name: calibrationGate, BucketPower
sections.title: Pass or fail gate and power shape
sections.what: Checks every band with at least 200 samples and passes only if none is more than 5 points off. Returns the failing bands and how many were checked. Also defines the power result shape.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed release check, as the header says.
sections.watch_out: Bands with fewer samples are not checked, and if none qualify the gate passes without checking anything.

sections.name: normalCdf
sections.title: Normal curve chance function
sections.what: Calculates the chance that a standard normal value falls below a number, approximated to within about 0.00000015.
sections.why: Likely reason: the power calculation needs it, and the standard formula is approximated rather than built in.
sections.watch_out: A similar helper exists in the basketball model, so a fix in one may need copying to the other.

sections.name: gatePower
sections.title: Power check for the gate
sections.what: For each band, estimates how much the observed rate would vary by chance when samples from the same match share an outcome. Also estimates the chance a perfectly calibrated model passes each band and all bands together.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows whether the gate can tell good calibration from bad. The code treats bands as independent.
sections.watch_out: Treating bands as independent is an assumption, so the overall pass chance is only an estimate.

summary: Adjusts predicted win chances so they match what really happened, and checks that every 10-point band is within 5 points of its observed rate.
purpose: Keeps the app's probabilities honest, and blocks a release when they are not.
why: The header describes isotonic recalibration and a calibration gate, a fixed check that must pass.
how: Sorts samples by predicted chance, merges neighbouring groups that break the rising trend, then maps any predicted chance to a corrected one by straight-line steps between points. The gate checks each band with enough samples. A power calculation estimates how often a good model would pass.
inputs: Samples of predicted chance and outcome (0 or 1), with optional weights and cluster names for the power check.
outputs: A correction map, the 10-point band results, a pass or fail gate result, and power figures.
risks: Bands with too few samples are skipped, so the gate can pass with little checking. Samples from the same match are related, so treating them as separate overstates confidence.
debug: If the gate fails, read the failing bands it lists. If the correction looks wrong, check the sample order and weights. Empty input throws an error.
